cases.title: Best Power Station for a Sump Pump: Which Models Start a 1/2-HP Pump
cases.subtitle: Surge, cycles per hour and the safe way to connect
cases.excerpt: Which power stations start a 1/2-HP sump pump, how many cycles you get per charge, and why hard-wired pumps need an electrician.
cases.body_md:
# Best Power Station for a Sump Pump

A 1/2-HP sump pump pulls about 900 W running and up to 2,500 W for a second at start-up, so surge matters more than capacity.

> **Safety:** Backfeeding a panel, double-male "suicide" cords and dryer-outlet hookups can electrocute line workers. A hard-wired sump pump needs a transfer switch or interlock installed by a licensed electrician.

## How we picked

We compared manufacturer surge ratings and usable capacity; we did not run our own tests.

| Station | Surge (W) | Cycles per charge |
|---|---|---|
| [Station A](/product/B0AAAAAAA1) | 3600 | 40 |
| [Station B](/product/B0AAAAAAA2) | 2400 | 22 |

## What not to do

- Backfeed through a dryer outlet
- Run a gas generator in the garage
- Bypass the BMS to charge a cold battery

Plug the pump's cord straight into the station. See [the compatibility hub](/compat/station-a) for cables.

faqs.question: Can I run my sump pump during a winter storm outage?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the station's surge rating clears the pump's start-up draw. Plug the pump in directly; never backfeed the house.

cases.title: Best Power Station for a Winter Outage
cases.excerpt: Which power stations keep a fridge, a router and phones running through a winter outage, and how to connect them safely.
cases.body_md:
# Best Power Station for a Winter Outage

A winter outage is mostly about the fridge, a router and phones. A 2,000 Wh station runs a full-size fridge for about 13 hours and keeps phones and a router going for days.

> **Safety:** Never backfeed your home through a dryer or wall outlet, and never use a double-male cord: either can electrocute a utility line worker.

## What we compared

We compared manufacturer capacity, surge and cold-weather charging specs; we did not run our own tests.

| Station | Capacity (Wh) | Surge (W) |
|---|---|---|
| [Station A](/product/B0AAAAAAA1) | 2048 | 4000 |
| [Station B](/product/B0AAAAAAA2) | 1024 | 2400 |

## Keeping the furnace safe

Gas furnaces need electricity for the blower, and the blower is hard-wired. Connecting a station to it takes a transfer switch or interlock installed by a licensed electrician; plug appliances straight into the station instead.

## Cold-weather charging

LiFePO4 cells should not charge below freezing. Pick a station with self-heating, and never bypass the BMS to force a cold charge.

## Generators

Never run a gas generator indoors or in an attached garage. Keep it outdoors, at least 20 feet from doors and windows.

faqs.question: Can I plug my furnace into a power station?
faqs.answer: Not with a plug: furnace blowers are hard-wired. Have a licensed electrician install a transfer switch or interlock, and never backfeed through an outlet.
